body:
# Chart — Technical Reference

Complete reference for `@filemark/chart` + its integration into
`@filemark/mdx`. Intended as the source-of-truth for info-string
grammar, plug-in contracts (renderers / palettes / formatters),
data-pipeline, and theming.

- Package: `@filemark/chart` (`packages/chart/`)
- Architecture: `packages/chart/ARCHITECTURE.md`
- Integration: `@filemark/mdx` — see `packages/mdx-viewer/src/MDXViewer.tsx`
  (new chart lang-branch + `chart` tag handler)
- Showcase: `examples/chart-full.md`

---

## 1. Goals

- **Interactive charts from markdown.** ` ```chart `, ` ```bar `,
  ` ```line `, ` ```pie `, ` ```area `, ` ```scatter ` fenced blocks
  render interactive charts via `recharts`.
- **Same grammar as datagrid.** Info-string flags / `<Tag>` attrs /
  `src=` AssetResolver path — authors learn once, use everywhere.
- **Pluggable from top to bottom.** Chart types, palettes, formatters
  — all lookup via registries; adding a new chart type is one file +
  one `registerChartType()` call, with zero edits to central code.
- **Zero bundle cost when unused.** `recharts` is dynamic-imported on
  first mount; docs with no charts pay 0 KB of chart code.
- **Accessibility in v1.** Every chart ships an `aria-label`,
  SR-friendly tooltip role, and an optional data-table fallback via
  `@filemark/datagrid`.

---

## 2. Authoring model

Two entry points mirror the datagrid's exactly.

### 2.1 Fenced block

````md
```chart type=bar x=region y=revenue title="Q2 revenue"
region,revenue
North,9380
South,10650
```
````

Lang tag aliases the default type — use any of ` ```chart `,
` ```bar `, ` ```line `, ` ```pie `, ` ```area `, ` ```scatter `.
Without `type=`, the fence lang wins.

### 2.2 `<Chart>` tag

```md
<Chart
  src="./sales.csv"
  type="line"
  x="month"
  y="users,revenue"
  title="Growth"
  smooth
  show-legend />
```

Same rules as `<Datagrid>` — src-based only (HTML attrs can't hold
multi-line CSV). Always close the tag explicitly
(`<Chart …></Chart>` or `<Chart … />`, but tag-with-close is safer
given GFM parsers' self-closing quirks).

---

## 3. Info-string grammar

Shell-ish tokenizer identical in spirit to the datagrid's:
whitespace-split, quotes respected, parens group internal whitespace.

### 3.1 Global flags

| Flag | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `type=<bar\|line\|pie\|area\|scatter\|funnel\|radar\|…>` | lang tag, else `bar` | Which renderer from the registry. Custom types registered at runtime work too. |
| `x=<col>` | first col | Category axis (bar/line/area). |
| `y=<col>[,<col>,…]` | second col | One or more series. |
| `by=<col>` | — | Long-form → wide-form pivot alternative to `y`. |
| `name=<col>` | aliases `x` on pie | Pie-specific slice labels. |
| `value=<col>` | aliases `y[0]` on pie | Pie-specific slice values. |
| `title=<text>` | — | Above-chart title. |
| `x-label=<text>` / `y-label=<text>` | inferred from col label | Axis titles. |
| `height=<px>` | 260 | Chart height. |
| `stacked` / `no-stacked` | off | Stack bars / areas. |
| `horizontal` / `no-horizontal` | off | Flip bar chart to horizontal (category on y). |
| `smooth` | off | Line: monotone spline instead of straight. |
| `show-dots` / `no-show-dots` | on for line, off for area | Per-point markers. |
| `show-grid` / `no-show-grid` | on | Cartesian grid lines. |
| `show-legend` / `no-show-legend` | on when > 1 series | Legend. |
| `show-x-axis` / `no-show-x-axis` | on | Toggle x-axis. |
| `show-y-axis` / `no-show-y-axis` | on | Toggle y-axis. |
| `show-table` | off | Opt-in a11y data-table fallback below the chart (uses `@filemark/datagrid`). |
| `donut` | off | Pie → donut (inner radius). |
| `show-total` | off | Donut-only: center label with sum. |
| `reference-line=<number>` | — | Horizontal dashed line. |
| `sort=<col>[:asc\|desc]` | file order | Sort before plotting. |
| `limit=<n>` | — | Top-n after sort (long-tail trimming). |
| `colors=<tone1,tone2,…>` | palette default | Semantic tones (`primary/success/warn/danger/info/secondary/muted`) or hex. One per series. |
| `palette=<name>` | `default` | Switch palette registered via `registerPalette()`. Built-in: `default`, `colorblind` (Okabe-Ito). |
| `annotations=<x1:label1,x2:label2,…>` | — | Dashed vertical markers on bar/line/area charts. Colon separates x-value from optional label; commas separate entries. |
| `src=<path>` | — | Absolute URL (direct fetch) or relative (via AssetResolver). |
| `delimiter=<char>` | `,` | Parse delimiter. |
| `header` / `no-header` | on | First row is header. |

### 3.2 Per-column format specs

| Flag | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `format:<col>=auto` | `format:revenue=auto` | Infer from col type (default for every col). |
| `format:<col>=number[(max-digits)]` | `format:revenue=number(0)` | Integer or N-fraction-digit locale number. |
| `format:<col>=currency(<ISO>)` | `format:spend=currency(USD)` | `Intl.NumberFormat` currency. |
| `format:<col>=percentage` | `format:rate=percentage` | Auto-scale 0..1 → ×100. |
| `format:<col>=filesize` | `format:size=filesize` | Auto K/M/G/T. |
| `format:<col>=date` | `format:day=date` | Short locale date. |
| `format:<col>=<custom>` | `format:ms=duration` | Any name registered via `registerFormat(name, fn)`. |

Unknown flag → `console.warn` with the token; chart still renders.
Rule 3 — skeleton honesty.

---

## 4. Plug-in contracts

Three separate registries. Each is keyed by a string; consumers look
up by string; plug-in authors register-as-they-go. Full TS shapes
in `packages/chart/src/types.ts`.

### 4.1 `ChartRenderer` — chart types

```ts
interface ChartRenderer<Shape = unknown> {
  readonly type: string;
  transform(columns, rows, options): ChartData<Shape>;
  render(ctx: ChartRenderContext<Shape>): ReactElement;
  validate?(options, columns): string[];
  readonly defaultOptions?: Partial<ChartOptions>;
}
```

One file under `packages/chart/src/renderers/`. Registers itself at
module-load time via `registerChartType(renderer)`. Built-ins:
`bar`, `line`, `pie`, `area`. Custom types drop in without touching
any central file:

```ts
import { registerChartType } from "@filemark/chart";
registerChartType({
  type: "radar",
  transform: transformCategorical,
  render: ({ data, recharts, palette }) => <recharts.RadarChart …/>,
});
```

### 4.2 `PaletteResolver` — colors

```ts
interface PaletteResolver {
  series(i: number): string;      // zero-indexed, wraps around
  tone(name: string): string;     // semantic name → color
  tones(): string[];              // list of available tones
}
```

Built-in tones: `primary`, `success`, `warn`, `info`, `danger`,
`secondary`, `muted`. Register more palettes:

```ts
registerPalette("brand", {
  series: (i) => BRAND_COLORS[i % BRAND_COLORS.length],
  tone: (n) => BRAND_TONES[n] ?? "currentColor",
  tones: () => Object.keys(BRAND_TONES),
});
```

Author opt-in via `palette=brand` or per-series via
`colors=primary,danger,#0ea5e9`. Default palette uses `var(--…)`
shadcn tokens so theme-switching re-skins every chart automatically.

### 4.3 `FormatResolver` — values

```ts
type FormatSpec =
  | { kind: "auto" }
  | { kind: "number"; maxFractionDigits?: number }
  | { kind: "currency"; code: string }
  | { kind: "percentage" }
  | { kind: "filesize" }
  | { kind: "date"; pattern?: string }
  | { kind: string; [arg: string]: unknown };

interface FormatResolver {
  format(value: unknown, spec: FormatSpec, col?: Column): string;
}
```

Custom formatter:

```ts
registerFormat("duration", (value) => formatSeconds(Number(value)));
// Author: format:buildTime=duration
```

---

## 5. Pipeline

```
 ```chart type=bar …  ──▶ remarkCodeMeta copies meta → hast data-meta
                      ──▶ MDXViewer.components.code sees lang ∈ CHART_LANGS
                      ──▶ <ChartBlock source meta options … />
                      ──▶ parseChartInfoString(meta, {defaultType: lang})
                             → ChartOptions
                      ──▶ ChartFromText (uses datagrid parseCSV)
                             → { columns, rows }
                      ──▶ Chart looks up registry.get(options.type)
                      ──▶ renderer.transform(columns, rows, options)
                             → ChartData<Shape>
                      ──▶ renderer.render(ctx) inside <ChartContainer>

 <Chart src=… type=… />
                      ──▶ MDXViewer.components.chart receives HTML attrs
                      ──▶ attrsToChartOptions(p) → ChartOptions
                      ──▶ <ChartBlock source="" options assets … />
                      ──▶ ChartBlock fetches src (absolute fetch / AssetResolver)
                      ──▶ downstream identical to fence path
```

---

## 6. Bundle behavior

- `@filemark/chart` dist: ~37 KB ESM (gz'd much smaller). Includes
  registries, renderers' JSX, tooltips, transforms.
- `recharts`: ~50 KB gz, **dynamic-imported** via `loadRecharts()`.
  First `<Chart>` on the page triggers the import; cached via a
  module-level Promise so subsequent charts reuse it instantly.
- Docs with zero charts never mount `<Chart>` and never call
  `loadRecharts()` → 0 KB recharts cost.
- `RechartsProvider` + `useRecharts()` hook ship one module of
  recharts for the whole tree — siblings don't race or re-import.

---

## 7. Theming

- Every renderer reads colors from the resolved `PaletteResolver`.
- Default palette maps semantic tones to `var(--…)` shadcn tokens
  where possible (primary / secondary / muted) with oklch fallbacks
  for tones shadcn doesn't ship (success / warn / danger / info).
- Axis strokes / ticks use `stroke="currentColor"` — inherits text
  color, which flips with the theme attribute (`data-theme="dark"`).
- Tooltip uses `bg-popover` / `text-popover-foreground` (shadcn).
- `<Chart>` has zero hard-coded hex colors. Swapping `ThemeProvider`
  mode re-skins every chart without a re-render.

---

## 8. Accessibility

- **Always:** `<figure role="figure" aria-label="…">` wraps every
  chart. The label derives from `title` when present, else a
  deterministic summary from `options.type + series + x` via
  `chartAriaLabel()`.
- **Tooltip:** `role="tooltip"` + `aria-live` implicit via SR-friendly
  `<div>` with semantic text content (label + value per series).
- **`show-table` fallback:** opt-in data table using
  `@filemark/datagrid` below the chart. Render the same rows in a
  compact grid so screen readers traverse semantic `<table>`.
- **Keyboard navigation through points:** not yet — v2 item. For now
  tab-able via the `<figure>` focus + the underlying SVG's built-in
  focus when `show-table` is on and screen-readers prefer the table.

---

## 9. Shipped renderers (v1.1)

- `bar` — vertical or horizontal bars, single / multi-series, stacking.
- `line` — straight or smooth (monotone spline), dots toggleable,
  multi-series.
- `area` — single or stacked area, smooth by default, dots optional.
- `pie` — standard pie or donut; `show-total` center label; automatic
  label-truncation for long names + label-skip for tiny slices
  (< 4%).
- `scatter` — `{x, y}` points, multi-series via `by=<col>`.
- `funnel` — conversion stages + drop-off, with right-side label list.
- `radar` — multi-attribute polar comparison, filled polygons per
  series.

## 10. Plug-in validation

Every built-in renderer implements `validate(options, columns)`:

- `validateCategorical` — used by `bar` / `line` / `area` / `scatter`
  / `radar`. Warns when `x`, `by`, or any `y[]` column isn't present
  in the data; warns when `y[]` column isn't numeric.
- `validatePie` — used by `pie` / `funnel`. Warns when `name` /
  `value` columns are missing or `value` isn't numeric.

Warnings that indicate a **fatal misconfig** (missing column) bubble
up to a visible `<ChartErrorCard>` inside `ChartContainer` — authors
see the problem on-screen, not just in DevTools. Non-fatal warnings
render the chart normally but log to console. Rule 3 — skeleton
honesty. Custom renderer authors can reuse the shared validators
(`warnIfMissing`, `warnIfMissingList`, `warnIfNotNumeric`) via the
public barrel.

## 11. SVG export

Every chart renders inside a `<ChartContainer>` which adds a hover-
reveal **SVG** button to the title bar. Click → serializes the inner
`<svg>` element (recharts renders natively to SVG), inlines the
current computed `color` + `background` to preserve styling outside
the page context, and downloads a `.svg` of the title as filename.

PNG export is not shipped yet — requires a rasterizer (html-to-image
or canvg) and wasn't worth the bundle cost for v1. SVG opens cleanly
in every modern tool.

## 12. Backlog (ranked by expected use × effort)

Every item below is spec'd well enough to pick up cold. None require
changes to the plug-in core — renderers are files, palettes /
formatters / types are registries.

### Tier A — high-value, small effort (~½ day each)

- **Stat cards** — `<Stat title="DAU" value="12,480" delta="+15%" />`
  or `<Stats src="./kpis.csv" />`. Tiny renderer, huge impact for
  summary docs. Properly lives alongside `@filemark/chart` but could
  be its own package. Reuses palette + formatter registries.
- **Dual y-axis** — `y2=<col>` paired with `y=<col>`. Mixed-scale
  series (e.g. revenue + churn rate). Recharts supports `yAxisId`
  first-class; wire up in bar / line / area renderers.
- **PNG export** — add alongside the existing SVG button. One tiny
  dep (`html-to-image` ~8 KB). Dropdown: SVG · PNG · data URL to
  clipboard.
- **Stacked-percent bars** — `stacked=percent` normalizes each bar
  to 100%. Common ask for part-whole analysis. One-line tweak inside
  the bar renderer's recharts props.

### Tier B — power features, medium effort (1–2 days each)

- **Brush / zoom** — per-chart opt-in flag; drag-to-select an
  x-range on long time-series. Recharts ships `<Brush>`.
- **Small-multiples / facet** — `facet=<col>` renders a grid of
  mini-charts, one per distinct value. Works for any categorical
  chart type with minor wrapper component.
- **CSV cache interop** — memoize `parseCSV` keyed by
  `(src, delimiter)` so a datagrid + chart on the same file parse
  once. Lift into `@filemark/core` or a shared `@filemark/csv` pkg.
- **Persisted chart state** via `StorageAdapter` — zoom level, hidden
  series, etc. Parallels the datagrid's sort/filter persistence.
- **Toolbar density control** — compact / comfy / relaxed padding
  preset toggled from the toolbar.

### Tier C — additional chart types (1 day each)

Each slots into the existing plug-in registry without touching core
code; just a new `renderers/<type>.tsx` file.

- **Treemap** — hierarchical part-whole, recharts native.
- **Heatmap** — two-axis color-scale matrix. No recharts primitive;
  hand-roll via SVG rects or pull in `visx-heatmap` (~15 KB).
- **Sankey** — flow / conversion-path diagram, recharts native.

### Tier D — accessibility + cross-chart (real work)

- **Keyboard nav through data points** — tab into chart, arrows step
  across points, space announces value to screen reader. Needs focus
  management in every renderer. Several hours per renderer.
- **Cross-chart synced tooltips** — for dashboards with multiple
  charts on the same x-axis. Shared React context + coordinated
  hover state. Meaningful work to design the API.

### Tier E — nice-to-haves (incremental polish)

- **`reference-area=<from:to>`** — shaded bands for highlighting
  x-range intervals.
- **`trendline`** — linear-regression overlay on scatter / line.
- **Animations** — currently explicitly disabled (`isAnimationActive=
  false`) to avoid re-render flicker on the shared recharts
  lazy-load path. Could be re-enabled once transitions are tested
  under lazy-load + theme-switching without jank.
- **Chart filename** — author-supplied export filename instead of
  the auto-derived `<title>.svg`.
- **Custom data-label formatters** on bars / pie slices (distinct
  from tooltip + axis tick formatters).

### What's NOT on the backlog (explicit non-goals)

- **MDX JSX expressions inside chart props** — MV3 CSP bans
  `unsafe-eval`; stays non-goal. Props stay string-valued on the
  `<Chart>` tag.
- **Chart editing inside Filemark** — it's a reader, not a vis
  editor. Authors edit the CSV / markdown; the chart renders.
- **Real-time streaming** — no WebSocket / SSE data feeds. Charts
  render static CSV + can re-read via auto-refresh; that's enough.
- **3D / WebGL charts** — not worth the bundle cost or the
  accessibility regression.

## 13. How to pull a backlog item into a build slot

1. Move its bullet from §12 into a new `TASKS.md` milestone (e.g. "M9
   — Chart v1.2 (stat cards + dual axis + stacked-percent)").
2. Mark status in this doc `⟶ in progress`.
3. On ship: move to the "shipped" column of `ROADMAP.md` §1 (pillar
   1), delete the bullet from §12, add a short line to §9 (shipped
   renderers) or the appropriate flag table if it's a new option.
4. Update `examples/chart-full.md` with a dedicated demo section —
   mirror the existing per-type/per-flag layout.

---

## 14. Related docs

- `packages/chart/ARCHITECTURE.md` — internal design and the contract
  every plug-in obeys. Read this before adding a new chart type /
  palette / formatter.
- `CHART_PLAN.md` — original plan (what / why).
- `DATAGRID.md` — reference pattern; chart mirrors its info-string
  grammar + `<Tag>` / fence authoring + `AssetResolver` integration.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` §11 — where the new lang-branch + tag handler slot
  into `MDXViewer`.
- `ROADMAP.md` pillar 1 (data) — chart is the second shipped
  component after the datagrid.
